lesson_title: Shared Bricks: HCF and LCM Without Guessing
hook_text: 360 sweets, 84 packets of chips, identical party packs. How many packs? No guessing — bricks.
clip_script: Lay the two brick rows side by side. 360: 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5. 84: 2, 2, 3, 7. Now pick out the bricks that appear in BOTH rows. A 2 in both — take it. Another 2 in both — take it. A third 2? Only 360 has one, so no. A 3 in both — take it. The 5 belongs to 360 alone; the 7 belongs to 84 alone. Shared bricks: 2, 2, 3. Multiply: 12. That 12 is the highest common factor, and it answers the problem: 12 packs, each with 30 sweets and 7 packets of chips. Nothing left over, and no bigger number could do it.
visual_style: Two rows of coloured Lego bricks slide side by side; matching bricks light up in pairs and lift out into a third row that multiplies to a glowing 12, while the lonely 5 and 7 bricks dim.
pacing: Steady brick-by-brick matching, then a quick snap to the answer.
